newsitem.title: USA: FED SEEN ADDING RESERVES THROUGH 4-DAY SYSTEM RPS.
newsitem.headline: FED SEEN ADDING RESERVES THROUGH 4-DAY SYSTEM RPS.

text.p: The Federal Reserve looks to kick off the second half of its two-week maintenance period on Thursday by adding reserves into the banking system via four-day fixed system repurchase agreements.

Analysts project around a $6 billion a day add need for the rest of the period, which rises to $8 billion in the period beginning August 14. With no outstanding RPs, the Fed is almost sure to enter the open market, they said.

"A four-day fixed system RP seems the most likely operation," according to MCM MoneyWatch. It would carry through the weekend but still leave ample room for adjustments in the final days of the maintenance period.

They noted that seven-day system RPs cannot be ruled out, "but in the past few days the Fed appears to have been approaching its add need cautiously, perhaps because of uncertainty about its size and hence may not want to commit itself through the end of the maintenance period with a seven-day operation."
On Wednesday, the Fed stayed out of the open market.
Federal funds were trading at the 5-1/2 percent target in early trading.
